caption: Repeater-lock D latch, 4 blocks (track memory census): the data input feeds repeater M (on stone) whose output is q; the enable input feeds a second repeater L pointing into M's side. While L is on M is locked and holds q; while it is off M follows d. Transparent while e is OFF (`enable low`), latency 4 gt.

Dropper RS latch, 4 blocks (track memory): droppers A (facing east) and B (facing west) face each other and hold one stone. s (next to A) fires A and the stone goes to B; r (next to B) fires B and it comes back; firing the empty one does nothing, so repeated s or r change nothing. A comparator on stone reads B: q is its output (1). Latency 6 gt (dropper 4 + comparator 2).

D latch, enable high, 5 blocks (track memory): repeater M carries d to q; comparator C in subtract mode points into M's side, with a redstone block behind it (15) and the enable input at its side, so C gives 15 - e: M is locked (holds q) while e is off and follows d while e is on. Latency 4 gt.

Counter 3, dropper corner ring, 8 blocks (track memory): the input cell touches three droppers on three axes (east, up, south); between each pair a hopper carries the stone on to the next dropper (dropper up -> hopper west -> dropper south -> hopper down -> dropper east -> hopper north). Each pulse fires all three; only the one holding the stone moves it, and its hopper delivers it after all three have fired, so the stone advances one dropper per pulse whatever the firing order. The comparator reads the east dropper: on during one pulse window in three (level style).
